name: Arty Party
description: Painters, sculptors, materials and the British art world.

words.bacon: Francis Bacon, the Dublin-born London painter of screaming popes.
words.freud: Lucian Freud, painter of unflinching portraits and grandson of Sigmund.
words.lowry: L. S. Lowry, painter of Salford's matchstick men and matchstick cats and dogs.
words.blake: William Blake, London poet, painter and printmaker of fiery visions.
words.riley: Bridget Riley, whose op art seems to ripple before your eyes.
words.hirst: Damien Hirst, who put a tiger shark in formaldehyde.
words.moore: Henry Moore, the Yorkshire sculptor of great reclining figures.
words.crome: John Crome, founder of the Norwich School of painters.
words.watts: G. F. Watts, Victorian painter with his own gallery at Compton in Surrey.
words.perry: Grayson Perry, the Essex potter who won the 2003 Turner Prize.
words.ofili: Chris Ofili, who won the 1998 Turner Prize with paintings resting on elephant dung.
words.quinn: Marc Quinn, who sculpted his own head from his frozen blood.
words.kitaj: R. B. Kitaj, who gave the 'School of London' painters their name.
words.piper: John Piper, painter of moody churches and the Coventry Cathedral baptistery window.
words.grant: Duncan Grant, Bloomsbury painter who decorated Charleston farmhouse with Vanessa Bell.
words.monet: Claude Monet, who painted the Houses of Parliament in London fog again and again.
words.manet: Édouard Manet, whose A Bar at the Folies-Bergère hangs at the Courtauld in London.
words.degas: Edgar Degas, painter and sculptor of ballet dancers.
words.klimt: Gustav Klimt, the Viennese painter of The Kiss, glittering with gold leaf.
words.munch: Edvard Munch, the Norwegian painter of The Scream.
words.ernst: Max Ernst, the Surrealist who made pictures by rubbing over textures (frottage).
words.bosch: Hieronymus Bosch, painter of The Garden of Earthly Delights.
words.durer: Albrecht Dürer, German master of the woodcut, famous for his rhinoceros.
words.steen: Jan Steen, painter of rowdy Dutch homes. The Dutch still call a messy house 'a Jan Steen household'.
words.kahlo: Frida Kahlo, the Mexican painter of searing self-portraits.
words.nolde: Emil Nolde, German Expressionist of blazing colour.
words.macke: August Macke, German Expressionist of bright, sunny colour.
words.lippi: Filippo Lippi, the Florentine painter-monk of the early Renaissance.
words.piero: Piero della Francesca, whose Baptism of Christ hangs in the National Gallery.
words.koons: Jeff Koons, maker of giant, shiny balloon dogs.
words.leger: Fernand Léger, French painter of tubular, machine-like figures.
words.angel: The Angel of the North, Antony Gormley's steel giant above Gateshead.
words.venus: The Rokeby Venus by Velázquez, in the National Gallery.
words.snail: The Snail, Matisse's colourful paper cut-out in the Tate collection.
words.blast: BLAST, the shouty magazine of the British Vorticists, launched in 1914.
words.slade: The Slade School of Fine Art at University College London.
words.prado: Madrid's great museum, home of Velázquez's Las Meninas.
words.salon: The Paris Salon, the official exhibition every artist once fought to get into.
words.easel: The stand that holds a painting while you work. From the Dutch for donkey.
words.gesso: Chalky white primer brushed onto panels and canvas before painting.
words.sable: The finest watercolour brushes, made from sable hair.
words.umber: An earthy brown pigment. Raw and burnt umber sit on every palette.
words.sepia: A warm brown ink once made from cuttlefish.
words.ochre: Earth pigment in yellows and reds, used since cave painting.
words.glaze: A thin, see-through layer of oil paint laid over dry paint.
words.secco: Painting onto dry plaster, as opposed to true fresco on wet plaster.
words.tondo: A round painting or relief, like Michelangelo's Taddei Tondo at the Royal Academy.
words.putti: Chubby winged infants who flutter through Renaissance and Baroque art.
words.pieta: A scene of Mary holding the dead Christ.
words.fauve: A 'wild beast': the Fauves shocked Paris with blazing, unnatural colour.
words.naive: Art in a self-taught, childlike style.
words.motif: A recurring shape, figure or idea in a work of art.
words.mural: A painting made directly on a wall.
words.cameo: A small relief carved in layered shell or stone.
words.conte: Conté crayon, a hard stick of pigment for drawing.
words.hatch: To shade with fine parallel lines. Cross-hatching layers them.
words.tonal: Built from light and shade rather than colour.
words.genre: Genre painting shows scenes of everyday life.
words.chalk: Drawing chalk, used for sketches since the Renaissance.
words.resin: Natural gum used to make varnish and some paint mediums.
words.linen: The finest canvas, woven from flax.
